Course Code: ADL 101
Department: ADL
Course Name: Constitutional Law
Semester: Fall
Credits: 3
ECTS: 7
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Turkish
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: Online
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: -
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Öğr. Gör. Dr. Utku TOPCAN
Course Lecturer(s): Öğr. Gör. Ayça KÖKEN DİKMEN
Assistant(s): Araş. Gör. Afra Teren GÜRLÜLER
Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to give information to the students at vocational school level regarding the basic concepts and principles of constitutional law by handling the subjects such as the concept of constitution, organisation of the state, the duties, powers and functions of the state organs, the guarantees of the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Will have a general information  about the power and the limits of the power of state organ and fundamental rights and freedoms Will have an idea about state of law, human rights and democracy. Will be able to protect their constitutional rights. Will learn the basic concepts and principles about Constitutional Law Will have an idea about constitutional jurisdiction
Course Description: The subjects such as; concept of constitution, the concept of constitutional law,  elements of the states, types of states, forms of governmental systems, democracy and types of democracy, elections, fundamental rights and freedoms, foundation and functions of  of Turkish Grand National Assembly, the duties and responsibilities of president and council of ministers, regulatory administrative acts of executive power holders, extraordinary governing procedures and constitutional jurisdiction will be the content of this course.
Week 1: The Concept of Constitution and Constitutional Law
Week 2: Constitutional Jurisdiction and Constituent Authorithy
Week 3: Concept of State
Week 4: The Systems of States
Week 5: The Systems of Governments
Week 6: Democracy
Week 7: Elections
Week 8: Fundamental Rights and Freedoms
Week 9: Midterm
Week 10: Constitutional Developments in Turkey
Week 11: Basic Properties of Republican Administration at 1982 Constitution Act
Week 12: Fundamental Rights and Freedoms at 1982 Constitution Act
Week 13: The Foundation and Duties of Turkish Grand National Assembly
Week 14: Duties and Responsibilities of President and Council of Ministers
Week 15: Regulatory Administrative Acts of Executive Power Holders and Constitutional Jurisdiction
Week 16: Final exam
Course Notes/Textbooks: GÖZLER, Kemal, Kısa Anayasa Hukuku, Ekin Kitabevi, 2015
Suggested Readings/Materials: GÖREN, Zafer, Anayasa Hukuku, Yetkin Yayınları, 2015

Course Code: ADL 102
Department: ADL
Course Name: Civil Procedural Law
Semester: Spring
Credits: 3
ECTS: 6
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Turkish
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: face to face
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: -
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Öğr. Gör. Utku TOPCAN
Course Lecturer(s): Öğr. Gör. Utku TOPCAN
Assistant(s): -
Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to provide students with basic knowledge on the main concepts, principles and rules of the Law of Civil Procedure.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Students who successfully complete this course will be able to; define the basic concepts and principles of civil trial procedure. Discuss the procedure of opening a case according to the civil trial procedure and basic procedures for the first degree phase. Evaluate evidence in civil proceedings. Explain the ways of the law. Classify alternative dispute resolution methods.
Course Description: The main concepts, principles and rules of the Law of Civil Procedure, procedural actions in the first instance, higher legal remedies and alternative dispute resolutions will be covered in this course.
Week 1: Overview of the Course, Notion of Judiciary,  Turkish Judicial System
Week 2: Civil Courts, Actors in Judiciary
Week 3: Procedural Actions, Parties
Week 4: Intervention to Case, Main Principles of the Law of Civil Procedure
Week 5: Overview of Civil Lawsuit, Filing a Civil Lawsuit
Week 6: Defense, Preliminary Examination
Week 7: Midterm
Week 8: Trial, Proof, Legal Evidences
Week 9: Judgment and Operative Provisions
Week 10: Simple Procedure, Appeal (İstinaf)
Week 11: Appeal (Temyiz), Appeal for the Sake of Law, Retrial
Week 12: Litigation Costs, Legal Aid
Week 13: Provisional Legal Protection
Week 14: Alternative Dispute Resolutions and Arbitration, Individual Application to the Constitutional Court
Week 15: Revision
Week 16: Final Exam
Course Notes/Textbooks: Medeni Usul Hukuku - Temel Bilgiler, PEKCANITEZ, Hakan, ATALAY, Oğuz, ÖZEKES, Muhammet, Vedat Yay., 11. Bası, 2017.
Suggested Readings/Materials: ARSLAN, Ramazan, YILMAZ, Ejder, TAŞINAR AYVAZ, Sema, Medeni Usul Hukuku, Yetkin Yay., 3. Baskı, 2017.

Course Code: ADL 104
Department: ADL
Course Name: Administrative Law and Administrative Procedure
Semester: Spring
Credits: 3
ECTS: 5
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Turkish
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: face to face
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: -
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Dr.Öğretim Üyesi Mine KASAPOĞLU TURHAN
Course Lecturer(s): Dr.Öğretim Üyesi Mine KASAPOĞLU TURHAN
Assistant(s): Araş. Gör. Barış KARAHAN
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; will be able to explain basic principles and concepts related to administrative law. will be able to know the administrative organization of Turkey and the functions of administration. will be able explain the basic principles and features of the procedure of administrative jurisdiction will be able to explain the organization and the jurisdiction of Administrative Courts in Turkey will be able to learn the types of administrative cases and will be able to use this information during his career will be able to examine the decisions of administrative courts
Course Description: The following subjects will be held in this course:The concepts and basic principles of administrative law; origin, development and features of administrative law; sources of administrative law; the administrative organization of Turkey; administrative acts, actions and contracts; public service; administrative police;  the liability of administrative agencies; civil servants; public domain; the basic principles, features, rules of the procedure of administrative jurisdiction in Turkey; the types of administrative cases, appellate procedure.
Week 1: The Concept of Administration; The Origin, Development and Features of Administrative Law
Week 2: The Sources of Administrative Law, Constitutional Principles Affecting Administrative Law
Week 3: Central Administration, Local Governments, Functionally Decentralized Agencies
Week 4: Administrative Acts
Week 5: Public Service
Week 6: Administrative Police, Civil Servants
Week 7: Liability of Administrative Agencies, Public Domain
Week 8: Mid-term
Week 9: The Origin, Development, Features and Scope of Administrative Jurisdiction in Turkey; The Organization of Administrative Jurisdiction in Turkey; The Jurisdiction of Administrative Courts; the Court of Conflicts and the Types of Conflicts
Week 10: Action for Annulment
Week 11: Action for Damages
Week 12: Basic Principles of the Procedure of Administrative Jurisdiction; Jurisdiction of Administrative Courts, Parties in Administrative Courts
Week 13: Time Limits for Litigation  in Administrative Courts, The Conditions of Bringing a Lawsuit and the Procedure in Administrative Courts
Week 14: The Results of Litigation, The Methods and the Means of Proving in Administrative Jurisdicition, Appellate Procedure
Week 15: Review of the semester
Week 16: Final Exam
Course Notes/Textbooks: GÖZÜBÜYÜK Şeref, Yönetim Hukuku, 31.Bası, Turhan Kitabevi, Ankara 2012; GÖZLER Kemal, İdare Hukukuna Giriş, 18.Baskı, Ekin Yayınları, Bursa 2013; GÜNDAY Metin, İdare Hukuku, 10.Baskı, İmaj Yayınevi, Ankara 2013; GÖZÜBÜYÜK Şeref, Yönetsel Yargı, 32.Bası, Turhan Kitabevi, Ankara 2013; ÖZAY İlhan, Günışığında Yönetim 2, Yargısal Korunma , On İki Levha Yayınları,  İstanbul 2010; Bahtiyar Akyılmaz/Cemil Kaya/Murat Sezginer, İdari Yargı Mevzuatı, 6. Baskı, Seçkin Yayınları, Ankara 2013

Course Code: ADL 105
Department: ADL
Course Name: Keyboard Usage I
Semester: Fall
Credits: 2
ECTS: 4
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Turkish
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: -
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: -
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Öğr. Gör. Dr. Utku TOPCAN
Course Lecturer(s): Öğr. Gör. Hakkı CAN
Assistant(s): Araş. Gör. Barış KARAHAN
Course Objectives: To provide the students ability of typing ten-finger F keyboard in an efficient, fast and accurate way and typing 100 correct words in 5 minutes (1 point per).
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; To be able to exchange correspondence about his field by using the computer applications, to be able to store information, to be able to use the stored information. To be able to make transaction on the datas about his field by using the computer applications. To be able to prepare the required reports on the datas about his field by using the computer applications. To be able to prepare the required information or reports on the datas about his field by using the computer applications. To be able to use the current computer applications
Course Description: Standard Turkish keyboard (F keyboard) is to most efficient keyboard for using keyboard method with 10 fingers, without looking pursuant to Turkish language. Using computer keyboard techniques fast and efficient with 10 fingers, methodically is given to you with this lecture. Sitting position, position of arms, position of hands, position of fingers, position of feet and accurate using techniques of the letter keys are offered to you in detail and with pictures in these techniques. You must learn and use these techniques to increase your yield at all kinds of correspondences in your professional life and private life.
Week 1: History of keyboard (development in the world and Turkey), sorts, comparison of F and Q keyboards and superiorities of F keyboard.
Week 2: Sitting position, position of hands, movements not to do
Week 3: Basic line keys.
Week 4: Key exercises and rhythmic writing workings.
Week 5: Key exercises and rhythmic writing workings
Week 6: Key exercises and rhythmic writing workings
Week 7: Key exercises and rhythmic writing workings
Week 8: Key exercises and rhythmic writing workings
Week 9: Key exercises and rhythmic writing workings
Week 10: Text writing and detection of errors
Week 11: 3 and 5 minute’s speed exercise
Week 12: 3 and 5 minute’s speed exercise
Week 13: Periodic speed exercise
Week 14: Periodic speed exercise
Week 15: Periodic speed exercise
Week 16: Final

Semester: Spring
Credits: 3
ECTS: 6
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Turkish
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: face to face
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: -
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: -
Course Lecturer(s): Öğr. Gör. Utku TOPCAN
Assistant(s): -
Course Objectives: The object of this course is to enable students to have information on sources and basic concepts of civil law and its sub sections and law of persons which is one of the sub sections.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; 1. Know the basic concepts of civil law. 2. Recognize sub sections of civil law and make necessary interpretations. 3. Explain basic principles of law of persons. Differentiate natural persons and legal persons. 4. Explain the difference between legal and mental capacity. Know the limitation of persons in terms of capacity.
Course Description: The following subjects will be held in this course:The concept of civil law, law of persons concept of personality, real persons and legal persons, kinship, legal residence, associations, foundations.
Week 1: General Information
Week 2: Concept of Right
Week 3: Preliminary Provisions (Enforcement of Turkish Civil Code,Judical Discretion, Principle of Bone Fide)
Week 4: Perliminary Provisions ( Principle of Honesty, Burden of Proof,  Public Registers and Bills)
Week 5: Law of Persons (Real Persons)
Week 6: Law of Persons (Protection of Personality and Name, Register of Births, Deaths and Marriages)
Week 7: Law of Persons (Legal Entity, Associations and Foundations)
Week 8: Midterm exam
Week 9: Law of the Family ( Engagement, Marriage)
Week 10: Law of the Family (General Provisions on Marriage, Marrital Property,	Division of Matrimonial Property)
Week 11: Law of the Family (Adfinitas, Tutorship)
Week 12: Law of Inheritance (Legal Heirs)
Week 13: Law of Inheritance (Transfer of Heritage)
Week 14: Law of Property (Real Rights)
Week 15: Law of Property (Possession, Land Registry)
Week 16: Final Exam
Course Notes/Textbooks: AKINTÜRK, Turgut, ATEŞ, KARAMAN, Derya, Medeni Hukuk, 23. Baskı, İstanbul, 2017

Course Objectives: This course aims to reveal the the main principles of criminal law, the general theory of crime, implementation areas of criminal law and the concepts of punishment and  offenders under the contemporary legal system and in the light of hystory of Criminal Law
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Will be able to understand and evaluate the general principles and common provisions of criminal law that are set in the first 75 articles of Turkish Penal Code, Will be able to understand and evaluate the definition and elements of crime, Will be able to understand and evaluate the criminal consequences of crime (e.g. punishment and means of safety precautions).
Course Description: Instructing and teaching elements and ways of emergence of crime, legal consequences and basic issues of society, law, criminal within the framework of defitional problems of crime and application area of criminal law.

Week 8: Major crimes, Attempt,Complicity, Joinder of crimes

Week 13: Deferment of the Announcement of the Verdict, Remission, Limitation, Prepayment
Week 14: Review of the Semester
Week 15: Final Exams
Week 16: Final Exams

Course Code: ADL 203
Department: ADL
Course Name: Law of Obligations
Semester: Fall
Credits: 3
ECTS: 4
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Turkish
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: -
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: -
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Öğr. Gör. Dr. Utku TOPCAN
Course Lecturer(s): Öğr. Gör. Utku TOPCAN
Assistant(s): Araş. Gör. Hasan Özgür TÜRE
Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to provide students with knowledge on the general provisions of the Turkish Code of Obligations (n.6098), in light of doctrinal and judicial resources at the short cycle level.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Classify the subjects regulated by and within the Turkish Code of Obligations, Define the elements of “Obligatio”, Compare the sources of Obligatio (i.e. contract, tort and unjust enrichment), Explain the founder elements of contract, tort and unjust enrichment, Discuss the effects and consequences of debts, Discuss the consequences of the termination of debts.
Course Description: Turkish Code of Obligations general provisions, contract, tort and unjust enrichment, the effects and consequences of debts, the consequences of the termination of debts.
Week 1: Subject – Sources and Basic Principles of the Law of Obligations, The Terms Debt – Obligatio – Liability-  Imperfect Obligation- Private Law Defences and Objections
Week 2: Sources of Obligatio, Law of Contracts (I): Formation and Form of Contract
Week 3: Law of Contracts (II): Freedom of contract, Limitations to contract, Standardized Terms of Contract, Invalidity of Contract

Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to teach students general English at an elementary level (A1 – A2). By the end of the course, the students will have learned to understand and use present simple, present continuous and past simple tenses in communicative contexts. They will be able to skim and scan simple texts on a variety of topics and write a paragraph of 100-120 words on common topics. They will be able to ask and give information and give simple descriptions of people, things and places.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; communicate in simple and routine tasks and exchange information on familiar topics; read and understand short, simple texts and search for specific information; write an email, a postcard or  a short text to give information about present and past activities; catch the main point / missing parts in short, clear and simple messages or dialogues.
Course Description: This is a compulsory English course which provides basic language skills such as reading, writing, listening and speaking at the beginning level.
Week 1: Guessing the meaning of unknown words (childhood diaries, photo captions, memory notes) – Describing people, places, and times in the past – Writing a short paragraph about childhood
Week 2: Listening for main ideas and details (museum guides, short talks) – Using regular past tense verbs
Week 3: Skimming texts and identifying references (journals, event texts) – Talking about the past using irregular verbs
Week 4: Listening for main ideas and inferences (news, interviews) – Forming questions in the past tense
Week 5: Reading comparison texts – Distinguishing between past and present tenses – Writing a comparison of two communication tools
Week 6: Making inferences – Using comparative adjectives – Comparing objects orally
Week 7: Skimming informational texts – Using superlative structures with adjectives
Week 8: Midterm Exam
Week 9: Listening to plans – Using the going to structure – Talking about future plans
Week 10: Reading notices and maps – Using prepositions of place – Writing descriptions of object locations
Week 11: Using a/an/the – Talking about cultural events
Week 12: Reading personal profiles and advertisements – Using can/can’t – Writing about personal skills
Week 13: Using will – Making future predictions
Week 14: Using should/shouldn’t – Writing advice texts
Week 15: Talking about free-time activities using (love/like/hate/enjoy) structures
Week 16: FINAL

Course Objectives: This course aims to raise awareness of the use of grammatical structures in both English and Turkish and thereby enabling the students to use both languages accurately and appropriately.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Use simple and complex grammatical structures in English and Turkish accurately. Form grammatically-correct sentences and texts in English and Turkish. Translate sentences from English into Turkish by adhering to the rules of Turkish grammar. Course Description: The Turkish Sign Language Course is a program aimed at teaching effective\\ncommunication with individuals who have hearing impairments and\\nteaching sign language. Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to understand the theoretical and practical aspects of social media, effectively use digital communication tools, examine the impact of social media platforms on individuals and businesses, and develop skills to create successful social media strategies. Additionally, the course aims to provide knowledge about the effects of social media on content management, community building, and personal and corporate brand management.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; will be able to interpret the impact of social media on individuals and interpersonal relations, will be able to explain the importance of new media for brands, will be able to discuss the role of social media in digital communication, will be able to evaluate the role of social media in intercultural interactions, will be able to define the role of social media in digital marketing, will be able to manage social media campaigns.
Course Description: This course examines the development of social media, its key concepts, and its role in today’s digital world. It provides students with fundamental knowledge on how social media platforms function, content creation, sharing, community management, and the development of social media strategies. Additionally, the course covers topics such as the individual, corporate, and societal impacts of social media, digital marketing, data analytics, and ethical issues. The course aims to offer both theoretical knowledge and practical experience through hands-on applications.

Week 3: Web 2.0 and social media

Speech samples: - Ты не знаешь, что это / кто это / как его зовут?  - Я знаю, где аптека. - Я знаю, что аптека недалеко. - Ты знаешь, что такой Антон? - Как вы думаете / ты думашь, когда фильм? - Я думаю, что фильм в 5 часов.   2. Grammar: - verbs of the first conjugation (знать и думать); - complex sentences with conjunctions.
Week 12: 1. Revision of the previous week  2. Phonetics: •	reading of numerals 1-199; •	reading of hard and soft consonants in the middle as well as at the end of the words; •	reading the names of days of week.  3. Speech samples: - Это город. Здесь улицы, дома, проспекты... - Это мои друзья. Они студенты, спортсмены... - Это аудитория. Здесь книги, ручки, столы... - Чьи это вещи? – Это мои вещи. – Это ваши / наши/ твои вещи. - Сколько стоит рыба? - Рыба стоит 152 рубля / 181 рубль / 195 рублей. - Дайте, пожалуйста. - Это дорого.   2. Grammar: •	plural number of nouns and possessive pronouns; •	question words чей/ чья/ чьё/ чьи; •	second conjugation verbs in present tense; •	interrogative        sentences with question word Сколько;
Week 13: 1. Speech samples: - Я говорю по-русски медленно / быстро. - Я говорю по-немецки хорошо / плохо.  Вы читаете по-русски? - Да, читаю. Я неплохо   читаю по-русски. - Вы пишете по-английски? - Да, я хорошо пишу по-английски.   3.   Grammar:     •	using of adverbs in sentences. •	usage of adverbs по-русски, по-английски ... •	second conjugation verbs in present tense;
Week 14: 1. Revision of the previous week   2. Speech samples: - Почему он не очень хорошо говорит по-русски? - Потому что он иностранец. - Она смотрит фильм. - Он слушает музыку. - Что вы любите делать в свободное время? - Я люблю играть в футбол.  3.   Grammar:    •	comparison of the first and second verb groups; •	любить+infinitive •	compound sentences with conjunction потому что

ECTS: 3
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Spanish

Assistant(s): -
Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to make students gain receptive and productive skills at A1 level in the scope of the Common European Framework of Reference.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; By the end of this course students will be able to: 1.	Express themselves in simple sentences which are mainly isolated about familiar topics; 2.	Interact in a very simple conversation by asking questions, answering questions, initiating or responding to simple statements on familiar topics and / or situations. 3.	Follow simple, basic speech that is slow and carefully articulated. 4.	Analyze very basic listening texts with the highest frequency vocabulary on familiar topics at a very basic level. 5.	Produce very simple sentences about familiar topics using simple or basic linking devices.
Course Description: This course is designed for students to be able to introduce themselves; use classroom expressions and greetings; ask and answer questions about personal details; give a physical description of people and their personality; talk about family; express ability and opinions.
Week 1: Introduction: Introducing the teacher, the course and the evaluation system  UNIT 0: “In the Class””- Greeting and introducing self to others. Exchanging personal information.FLIPPED CLASSROOM CONTENT
Week 2: UNIT 1: “We” – Greetings and introducing  self to others.  Ask for the meaning and spelling of a  word.
Week 3: UNIT 1: “We” - Distinguish feminine and masculine nouns and adjectives, conjugate verbs Ser, Tener, Llamarse in the Present tense. Fill in forms with personal information
Week 4: UNIT 1: “We” – Give and ask for  personal information.  Confirm and correct  information. Places of work and numbers to 100.
Week 5: UNIT 2: “I want to learn Spanish” – Definite and  Indefinite articles. Form the plural of nouns and  adjectives.
Week 6: UNIT 2: “I want to learn Spanish” – Conjugate regular verbs in the Present tense. Express intentions and reasons. QUIZ
Week 7: UNIT 3: “Where is Santiago?” –Express existence,  location and  descriptions with Hay/Estar/Ser.
Week 8: MIDTERM EXAMS WEEK
Week 9: UNIT 4: “Which one do you prefer?” –  Talk about clothes and preferences.  Verb preferir.
Week 10: UNIT 4: “Which one do you prefer?” –  Demonstratives and some irregulars verbs as Ir
Week 11: UNIT 4: “Which one do you prefer?” – Express need  with Tener que + Infinitive verb.
Week 12: UNIT 5: “Your friends are my friends” – Express likes,  dislikes, interests, and hobbies.
Week 13: UNIT 5: “Your friends are my friends” – Make a  physical and personality description of people  taking into account noun and adjective agreement.
Week 14: Oral Exams
Week 15: Semester Review
Week 16: Final Exam

Credits: 4
ECTS: 4

Course Objectives: The course provides a general approach for analysis of the foundation of the Republic of Turkey under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Emphasizing military, political, sociocultural and economic developments, the course seeks to compare the sectoral reforms of the Ottoman State during the period of the decline of the Empire with the farreaching, radical and revolutionary attempts made by Atatürk which paved the way for the establishment of modern and civilized institutions in Turkey between 1920 and 1938.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Describe the actors and factors that determine the history Analyze the different roles of these actors and factors Interpret the concepts of independence, freedom and national sovereignty Evaluate the process of formation of the contemporary, democratic, secular and social state of Turkey Understand the importance of national unity and cohesion. Explain the national goals and objectives of the Republic of Turkey. Solve the problems that Turkish society will face with an Atatürkist approach.
Course Description: This course provides a general information of the events from the end of the 19. century until the end of the Turkish War of Independence and the signing of the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 and the following period until 1990’s.
Week 1: Course aim and related words
Week 2: The Reasons of the Collapse of Ottoman State   Ottoman Reforms
Week 3: The State of the Ottoman Empire in the Early 20th Century
Week 4: World War I and the Fall of the Ottoman Empire
Week 5: Ottoman State after Mudros Armistice
Week 6: Preparation for The National Struggle
Week 7: Opening and Works of the Turkish Grand National Assembly
Week 8: Midterm Exam
Week 9: Lausenne Peace Agreement and Political Reforms
Week 10: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 11: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 12: Foreign Policy of Atatürk Period  (1923-1938)
Week 13: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
Week 14: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
15: Review of the Semester
16: Review of the Semester
Course Notes/Textbooks: Hasan Mert, Nuri Karakaş, vd., Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Tarihi, Editör: Elçin Yılmaz, İzmir Ekonomi Üniversitesi Y ayınları, 2024.
Suggested Readings/Materials: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, Nutuk, Atatürk Araştırma Merkezi, Ankara 2005 Bernard Lewis, Modern Türkiye’nin Doğuşu, Ankara, 2017 Lord Kinross, Atatürk, İstanbul, 1981 Mahmut Goloğlu, Devrimler ve Tepkileri, İstanbul, 2009

Course Code: TRK 100
Department: AET
Course Name: Turkish
Semester: Spring
Credits: 4
ECTS: 4
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Turkish
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: -
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: Discussion Q&A Lecture / Presentation
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Öğr. Gör. Zarife Ekim SEVİNDİ
Course Lecturer(s): Dr. Öğr. Üyesi Mehmet AKKAYA Öğr. Gör. Zarife Ekim SEVİNDİ
Assistant(s): -
Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to show the students characteristics and rules of Turkish Language through examples; make them achieve the habit and skill of showing their emotions, thoughts, plans, impressions, observations, and experiences efficiently in writing and verbally; develop their vocabulary with the help of written and verbal texts; teach them the rules of comprehending the texts they read or programs they listen to accurately; develop their language skills which form the basis of the communication between individuals and populace.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; understand the rules of written expression, gain the ability to express their ideas effectively. learn the words forming sentences and recognize the importance of syntax. gain reading habit and read the book or attend events where comments from their perspective. acquire the stages of preparing scientific writing (collecting data, showing references, etc.). use communication tools -the form of petitions, official report, letters, etc. -for future life.
Course Description: Students will be taught how to use the written and verbal communication tools accurately and efficiently in this course. Various types of verbal and written statements will be examined through a critical point of view by doing exercises on understanding, telling, reading, and writing. Punctuation and spelling rules, which are basis of written statement, will be taught and accurate usage of these rules for efficient and strong expression will be provided. As for verbal statement, students will be taught how to use the body language, use accent and intonation elaborately, and use presentation techniques.
Week 1: Communication (Elements of Communication)
Week 2: Languages in the Wold and the Place of Turkish among World Languages
Week 3: Languages in the World and the Place of Turkish among World Languages
Week 4: Culture and Cultural Elements
Week 5: Writing Rules (Correctional Mark, Writing Some Words and Attachments, Where Lowercase Letters Are Used, Where Capital Letters Are Used)
Week 6: Writting And  Rules Of Punctuation Marks (Spelling of compound words, spelling of idioms, spelling of dilemmas, spelling of common words, spelling of foreign nouns)
Week 7: Punctuation Marks
Week 8: Composition and Forms of Expression
Week 9: Types of Writing (Official "Formal" Articles: Petition, Record, Decision)
Week 10: Writing Types (Official "Formal" Articles: Report, Business Letters, CV)
Week 11: Types of Writing: Articles Transmitting Thoughts and Information: Clause, Article, Criticism, Essay, Letter…)
Week 12: Types of Oral Expression (Open session, Symposium, Panel, Forum, Colloquium)
Week 13: Types of Oral Expression (Conference, Discourse)
Week 14: SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH AND EFFECTIVE PRESENTATION TECHNIQUES (Scientific Research)
Week 15: Semester Review
Week 16: Final Sınavı
Course Notes/Textbooks: Yakıcı, A., Yücel, M., (...)&Yelok,S. (2010). Türk Dili ve Kompozisyon Bilgileri, Yargı Publishing house, Ankara.
Suggested Readings/Materials: Korkmaz, Z. (2003). Türk Dili ve Kompozisyon Bilgileri, 6. Baskı, Ankara:YargıYayınevi.. Önen,A. (2007). Türkçeyi Türkçe Konuşmak, İnkılap Yayınevi, İstanbul.

Course Objectives: The course provides a general approach for analysis of the foundation of the Republic of Turkey under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Emphasizing military, political, sociocultural and economic developments, the course seeks to compare the sectoral reforms of the Ottoman State during the period of the decline of the Empire with the farreaching, radical and revolutionary attempts made by Atatürk which paved the way for the establishment of modern and civilized institutions in Turkey between 1920 and 1938.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Describe the actors and factors that determine the history Analyze the different roles of these actors and factors Interpret the concepts of independence, freedom and national sovereignty Evaluate the process of formation of the contemporary, democratic, secular and social state of Turkey Understand the importance of national unity and cohesion. Explain the national goals and objectives of the Republic of Turkey. Solve the problems that Turkish society will face with an Atatürkist approach.
Course Description: This course provides a general information of the events from the end of the 19. century until the end of the Turkish War of Independence and the signing of the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 and the following period until 1990’s.
Week 1: Course aim and related words
Week 2: The Reasons of the Collapse of Ottoman State   Ottoman Reforms
Week 3: The State of the Ottoman Empire in the Early 20th Century

Week 6: Preparation for The National Struggle
Week 7: Opening and Works of the Turkish Grand National Assembly
Week 8: Midterm Exam

Week 10: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 11: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 12: Foreign Policy of Atatürk Period  (1923-1938)
Week 13: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
Week 14: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
15: Review of the Semester
16: Review of the Semester

Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to show the students characteristics and rules of Turkish Language through examples; make them achieve the habit and skill of showing their emotions, thoughts, plans, impressions, observations, and experiences efficiently in writing and verbally; develop their vocabulary with the help of written and verbal texts; teach them the rules of comprehending the texts they read or programs they listen to accurately; develop their language skills which form the basis of the communication between individuals and populace.

Course Objectives: The course provides a general approach for analysis of the foundation of the Republic of Turkey under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Emphasizing military, political, sociocultural and economic developments, the course seeks to compare the sectoral reforms of the Ottoman State during the period of the decline of the Empire with the farreaching, radical and revolutionary attempts made by Atatürk which paved the way for the establishment of modern and civilized institutions in Turkey between 1920 and 1938.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Describe the actors and factors that determine the history Analyze the different roles of these actors and factors Interpret the concepts of independence, freedom and national sovereignty Evaluate the process of formation of the contemporary, democratic, secular and social state of Turkey Understand the importance of national unity and cohesion. Explain the national goals and objectives of the Republic of Turkey. Solve the problems that Turkish society will face with an Atatürkist approach.
Course Description: This course provides a general information of the events from the end of the 19. century until the end of the Turkish War of Independence and the signing of the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 and the following period until 1990’s.

Week 2: The Reasons of the Collapse of Ottoman State   Ottoman Reforms

Department: BNS
Course Name: Turkish
Semester: Spring
Credits: 4
ECTS: 4
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Turkish
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: -
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: Discussion Q&A Lecture / Presentation
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Öğr. Gör. Zarife Ekim SEVİNDİ
Course Lecturer(s): Dr. Öğr. Üyesi Mehmet AKKAYA Öğr. Gör. Zarife Ekim SEVİNDİ
Assistant(s): -
Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to show the students characteristics and rules of Turkish Language through examples; make them achieve the habit and skill of showing their emotions, thoughts, plans, impressions, observations, and experiences efficiently in writing and verbally; develop their vocabulary with the help of written and verbal texts; teach them the rules of comprehending the texts they read or programs they listen to accurately; develop their language skills which form the basis of the communication between individuals and populace.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; understand the rules of written expression, gain the ability to express their ideas effectively. learn the words forming sentences and recognize the importance of syntax. gain reading habit and read the book or attend events where comments from their perspective. acquire the stages of preparing scientific writing (collecting data, showing references, etc.). use communication tools -the form of petitions, official report, letters, etc. -for future life.
Course Description: Students will be taught how to use the written and verbal communication tools accurately and efficiently in this course. Various types of verbal and written statements will be examined through a critical point of view by doing exercises on understanding, telling, reading, and writing. Punctuation and spelling rules, which are basis of written statement, will be taught and accurate usage of these rules for efficient and strong expression will be provided. As for verbal statement, students will be taught how to use the body language, use accent and intonation elaborately, and use presentation techniques.
Week 1: Communication (Elements of Communication)
Week 2: Languages in the Wold and the Place of Turkish among World Languages
Week 3: Languages in the World and the Place of Turkish among World Languages
Week 4: Culture and Cultural Elements
Week 5: Writing Rules (Correctional Mark, Writing Some Words and Attachments, Where Lowercase Letters Are Used, Where Capital Letters Are Used)
Week 6: Writting And  Rules Of Punctuation Marks (Spelling of compound words, spelling of idioms, spelling of dilemmas, spelling of common words, spelling of foreign nouns)
Week 7: Punctuation Marks
Week 8: Composition and Forms of Expression
Week 9: Types of Writing (Official "Formal" Articles: Petition, Record, Decision)
Week 10: Writing Types (Official "Formal" Articles: Report, Business Letters, CV)
Week 11: Types of Writing: Articles Transmitting Thoughts and Information: Clause, Article, Criticism, Essay, Letter…)
Week 12: Types of Oral Expression (Open session, Symposium, Panel, Forum, Colloquium)
Week 13: Types of Oral Expression (Conference, Discourse)
Week 14: SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH AND EFFECTIVE PRESENTATION TECHNIQUES (Scientific Research)
Week 15: Semester Review
Week 16: Final Sınavı
Course Notes/Textbooks: Yakıcı, A., Yücel, M., (...)&Yelok,S. (2010). Türk Dili ve Kompozisyon Bilgileri, Yargı Publishing house, Ankara.
Suggested Readings/Materials: Korkmaz, Z. (2003). Türk Dili ve Kompozisyon Bilgileri, 6. Baskı, Ankara:YargıYayınevi.. Önen,A. (2007). Türkçeyi Türkçe Konuşmak, İnkılap Yayınevi, İstanbul.

Course Objectives: The course provides a general approach for analysis of the foundation of the Republic of Turkey under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Emphasizing military, political, sociocultural and economic developments, the course seeks to compare the sectoral reforms of the Ottoman State during the period of the decline of the Empire with the farreaching, radical and revolutionary attempts made by Atatürk which paved the way for the establishment of modern and civilized institutions in Turkey between 1920 and 1938.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Describe the actors and factors that determine the history Analyze the different roles of these actors and factors Interpret the concepts of independence, freedom and national sovereignty Evaluate the process of formation of the contemporary, democratic, secular and social state of Turkey Understand the importance of national unity and cohesion. Explain the national goals and objectives of the Republic of Turkey. Solve the problems that Turkish society will face with an Atatürkist approach.
Course Description: This course provides a general information of the events from the end of the 19. century until the end of the Turkish War of Independence and the signing of the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 and the following period until 1990’s.

Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to provide students with reading, writing, listening and speaking skills at the beginner level (A1 level) in English language.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Communicate at a basic level by asking and answering simple questions Answer questions about very short, simple texts by scanning for specific information, Write a short text including an email, a postcard and a paragraph of present activities by giving information about themselves and/or their immediate surroundings, Fill in forms with personal details, Recognise familiar words and very basic phrases about themselves, their family and immediate surroundings in a simple speech spoken at a slow pace.
Course Description: This is a compulsory English course which provides basic language skills such as reading, writing, listening and speaking at the beginning level.
Week 1: Introduction to the course
Week 2: Introduce oneself and others-Identify names, surnames, occupations from texts-Use greetings, list countries, numbers 0–30
Week 3: Extract names, countries from conversations-Use greetings and introductions with correct stress-Write basic personal information accurately
Week 4: Use have got and possessive adjectives-Identify key points in music texts	-Use nationality words and days of the week
Week 5: Recognize days, music types, languages, countries-Introduce self using "I am" / "I have got"-Write a forum introduction with correct structures
Week 6: Form present simple (I, you, we, they)-Identify family info in texts-Name family members and belongings
Week 7: Recognize family relationships-Describe family and answer questions clearly-Write about family using relevant vocabulary
Week 8: Use present simple (he, she, it); adverbs-Extract routine data from timetables-Use time phrases, daily routine words
Week 9: Extract routine details from conversations-Share someone’s routine using intonation-Describe routines using sequence and time words
Week 10: Use quantifiers with countable/uncountable nouns-Identify ingredients from recipes-Name food, meals, and drinks
Week 11: Recognize food and drinks in dialogue-Discuss meals clearly and naturally-Write about a favorite meal
Week 12: Use there is/are and prepositions of place-Identify room details in texts-Name furniture, rooms, town places
Week 13: Extract data on places and rooms-Describe rooms and towns with spatial accuracy-Write a room/town description
Week 14: Use present continuous -Extract product details from ads- Use clothing and shopping words
Week 15: Recognize clothing items and numbers-Describe clothing using present continuous-Write outfit descriptions
Week 16: Final Exam

Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to teach students general English at an elementary level (A1 – A2). By the end of the course, the students will have learned to understand and use present simple, present continuous and past simple tenses in communicative contexts. They will be able to skim and scan simple texts on a variety of topics and write a paragraph of 100-120 words on common topics. They will be able to ask and give information and give simple descriptions of people, things and places.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; communicate in simple and routine tasks and exchange information on familiar topics; read and understand short, simple texts and search for specific information; write an email, a postcard or  a short text to give information about present and past activities; catch the main point / missing parts in short, clear and simple messages or dialogues.
Course Description: This is a compulsory English course which provides basic language skills such as reading, writing, listening and speaking at the beginning level.
Week 1: Guessing the meaning of unknown words (childhood diaries, photo captions, memory notes) – Describing people, places, and times in the past – Writing a short paragraph about childhood
Week 2: Listening for main ideas and details (museum guides, short talks) – Using regular past tense verbs
Week 3: Skimming texts and identifying references (journals, event texts) – Talking about the past using irregular verbs
Week 4: Listening for main ideas and inferences (news, interviews) – Forming questions in the past tense
Week 5: Reading comparison texts – Distinguishing between past and present tenses – Writing a comparison of two communication tools
Week 6: Making inferences – Using comparative adjectives – Comparing objects orally
Week 7: Skimming informational texts – Using superlative structures with adjectives
Week 8: Midterm Exam
Week 9: Listening to plans – Using the going to structure – Talking about future plans
Week 10: Reading notices and maps – Using prepositions of place – Writing descriptions of object locations
Week 11: Using a/an/the – Talking about cultural events
Week 12: Reading personal profiles and advertisements – Using can/can’t – Writing about personal skills
Week 13: Using will – Making future predictions
Week 14: Using should/shouldn’t – Writing advice texts
Week 15: Talking about free-time activities using (love/like/hate/enjoy) structures
Week 16: FINAL

Course Objectives: The course provides a general approach for analysis of the foundation of the Republic of Turkey under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Emphasizing military, political, sociocultural and economic developments, the course seeks to compare the sectoral reforms of the Ottoman State during the period of the decline of the Empire with the farreaching, radical and revolutionary attempts made by Atatürk which paved the way for the establishment of modern and civilized institutions in Turkey between 1920 and 1938.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Describe the actors and factors that determine the history Analyze the different roles of these actors and factors Interpret the concepts of independence, freedom and national sovereignty Evaluate the process of formation of the contemporary, democratic, secular and social state of Turkey Understand the importance of national unity and cohesion. Explain the national goals and objectives of the Republic of Turkey. Solve the problems that Turkish society will face with an Atatürkist approach.
Course Description: This course provides a general information of the events from the end of the 19. century until the end of the Turkish War of Independence and the signing of the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 and the following period until 1990’s.
Week 1: Course aim and related words
Week 2: The Reasons of the Collapse of Ottoman State   Ottoman Reforms
Week 3: The State of the Ottoman Empire in the Early 20th Century
Week 4: World War I and the Fall of the Ottoman Empire
Week 5: Ottoman State after Mudros Armistice
Week 6: Preparation for The National Struggle
Week 7: Opening and Works of the Turkish Grand National Assembly
Week 8: Midterm Exam
Week 9: Lausenne Peace Agreement and Political Reforms
Week 10: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 11: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 12: Foreign Policy of Atatürk Period  (1923-1938)
Week 13: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
Week 14: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
15: Review of the Semester
16: Review of the Semester

Course Name: Turkish
Semester: Fall
Credits: 4
ECTS: 4
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: Turkish
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: -
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: Discussion Q&A Lecture / Presentation
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Öğr. Gör. Zarife Ekim SEVİNDİ
Course Lecturer(s): Dr. Öğr. Üyesi Mehmet AKKAYA Öğr. Gör. Zarife Ekim SEVİNDİ
Assistant(s): -
Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to show the students characteristics and rules of Turkish Language through examples; make them achieve the habit and skill of showing their emotions, thoughts, plans, impressions, observations, and experiences efficiently in writing and verbally; develop their vocabulary with the help of written and verbal texts; teach them the rules of comprehending the texts they read or programs they listen to accurately; develop their language skills which form the basis of the communication between individuals and populace.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; understand the rules of written expression, gain the ability to express their ideas effectively. learn the words forming sentences and recognize the importance of syntax. gain reading habit and read the book or attend events where comments from their perspective. acquire the stages of preparing scientific writing (collecting data, showing references, etc.). use communication tools -the form of petitions, official report, letters, etc. -for future life.
Course Description: Students will be taught how to use the written and verbal communication tools accurately and efficiently in this course. Various types of verbal and written statements will be examined through a critical point of view by doing exercises on understanding, telling, reading, and writing. Punctuation and spelling rules, which are basis of written statement, will be taught and accurate usage of these rules for efficient and strong expression will be provided. As for verbal statement, students will be taught how to use the body language, use accent and intonation elaborately, and use presentation techniques.
Week 1: Communication (Elements of Communication)
Week 2: Languages in the Wold and the Place of Turkish among World Languages
Week 3: Languages in the World and the Place of Turkish among World Languages
Week 4: Culture and Cultural Elements
Week 5: Writing Rules (Correctional Mark, Writing Some Words and Attachments, Where Lowercase Letters Are Used, Where Capital Letters Are Used)
Week 6: Writting And  Rules Of Punctuation Marks (Spelling of compound words, spelling of idioms, spelling of dilemmas, spelling of common words, spelling of foreign nouns)
Week 7: Punctuation Marks
Week 8: Composition and Forms of Expression
Week 9: Types of Writing (Official "Formal" Articles: Petition, Record, Decision)
Week 10: Writing Types (Official "Formal" Articles: Report, Business Letters, CV)
Week 11: Types of Writing: Articles Transmitting Thoughts and Information: Clause, Article, Criticism, Essay, Letter…)
Week 12: Types of Oral Expression (Open session, Symposium, Panel, Forum, Colloquium)
Week 13: Types of Oral Expression (Conference, Discourse)
Week 14: SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH AND EFFECTIVE PRESENTATION TECHNIQUES (Scientific Research)
Week 15: Semester Review
Week 16: Final Sınavı
Course Notes/Textbooks: Yakıcı, A., Yücel, M., (...)&Yelok,S. (2010). Türk Dili ve Kompozisyon Bilgileri, Yargı Publishing house, Ankara.
Suggested Readings/Materials: Korkmaz, Z. (2003). Türk Dili ve Kompozisyon Bilgileri, 6. Baskı, Ankara:YargıYayınevi.. Önen,A. (2007). Türkçeyi Türkçe Konuşmak, İnkılap Yayınevi, İstanbul.

Course Objectives: This course aims to prepare students for university education and campus life, while guiding them to develop the academic, social, and personal skills they will need throughout their university education.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; use the facilities provided by the academic and administrative units of the university, describe the academic skills such as notetaking, academic reading, accessing information, time management and analytical thinking, explain social skills such as effective communication and entrepreneurship, recognize their strengths and weaknesses using strategies such as goal setting, self-awareness, and mindfulness, they will be able to explain the habits they need to develop for their physical, mental, and spiritual health, as well as the behaviors they should avoid,
Course Description: The course will help students recognize the skills necessary for university life and personal development. These skills include self-awareness, goal setting, time management, effective communication, mindfulness, and analytical thinking. The course will also raise students' awareness of the habits essential for physical, mental, and spiritual health, as well as issues such as addiction and bullying.

Course Code: ING 101
Department: MINT
Course Name: English I
Semester: Fall
Credits: 3
ECTS: 3
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: English
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: -
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: Q&A Simulation Lecture / Presentation
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Öğr. Gör. Anıl UÇAK
Course Lecturer(s): Öğr. Gör. Ebru DEMİR
Assistant(s): -
Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to provide students with reading, writing, listening and speaking skills at the beginner level (A1 level) in English language.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Communicate at a basic level by asking and answering simple questions Answer questions about very short, simple texts by scanning for specific information, Write a short text including an email, a postcard and a paragraph of present activities by giving information about themselves and/or their immediate surroundings, Fill in forms with personal details, Recognise familiar words and very basic phrases about themselves, their family and immediate surroundings in a simple speech spoken at a slow pace.
Course Description: This is a compulsory English course which provides basic language skills such as reading, writing, listening and speaking at the beginning level.
Week 1: Introduction to the course
Week 2: Introduce oneself and others-Identify names, surnames, occupations from texts-Use greetings, list countries, numbers 0–30
Week 3: Extract names, countries from conversations-Use greetings and introductions with correct stress-Write basic personal information accurately
Week 4: Use have got and possessive adjectives-Identify key points in music texts	-Use nationality words and days of the week
Week 5: Recognize days, music types, languages, countries-Introduce self using "I am" / "I have got"-Write a forum introduction with correct structures
Week 6: Form present simple (I, you, we, they)-Identify family info in texts-Name family members and belongings
Week 7: Recognize family relationships-Describe family and answer questions clearly-Write about family using relevant vocabulary
Week 8: Use present simple (he, she, it); adverbs-Extract routine data from timetables-Use time phrases, daily routine words
Week 9: Extract routine details from conversations-Share someone’s routine using intonation-Describe routines using sequence and time words
Week 10: Use quantifiers with countable/uncountable nouns-Identify ingredients from recipes-Name food, meals, and drinks
Week 11: Recognize food and drinks in dialogue-Discuss meals clearly and naturally-Write about a favorite meal
Week 12: Use there is/are and prepositions of place-Identify room details in texts-Name furniture, rooms, town places
Week 13: Extract data on places and rooms-Describe rooms and towns with spatial accuracy-Write a room/town description
Week 14: Use present continuous -Extract product details from ads- Use clothing and shopping words
Week 15: Recognize clothing items and numbers-Describe clothing using present continuous-Write outfit descriptions
Week 16: Final Exam
Course Notes/Textbooks: SFL Materials

Course Code: ING 102
Department: MINT
Course Name: English II
Semester: Spring
Credits: 3
ECTS: 3
Prerequisites: None
Course Language: English
Course Type: Required
Course Level: Short Cycle
Mode of Delivery: -
Teaching Methods and Techniques of the Course: Q&A Lecture / Presentation
National Occupation Classification: -
Course Coordinator: Öğr. Gör. Anıl UÇAK
Course Lecturer(s): Öğr. Gör. Ebru DEMİR
Assistant(s): -
Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to teach students general English at an elementary level (A1 – A2). By the end of the course, the students will have learned to understand and use present simple, present continuous and past simple tenses in communicative contexts. They will be able to skim and scan simple texts on a variety of topics and write a paragraph of 100-120 words on common topics. They will be able to ask and give information and give simple descriptions of people, things and places.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; communicate in simple and routine tasks and exchange information on familiar topics; read and understand short, simple texts and search for specific information; write an email, a postcard or  a short text to give information about present and past activities; catch the main point / missing parts in short, clear and simple messages or dialogues.
Course Description: This is a compulsory English course which provides basic language skills such as reading, writing, listening and speaking at the beginning level.
Week 1: Guessing the meaning of unknown words (childhood diaries, photo captions, memory notes) – Describing people, places, and times in the past – Writing a short paragraph about childhood
Week 2: Listening for main ideas and details (museum guides, short talks) – Using regular past tense verbs
Week 3: Skimming texts and identifying references (journals, event texts) – Talking about the past using irregular verbs
Week 4: Listening for main ideas and inferences (news, interviews) – Forming questions in the past tense
Week 5: Reading comparison texts – Distinguishing between past and present tenses – Writing a comparison of two communication tools
Week 6: Making inferences – Using comparative adjectives – Comparing objects orally
Week 7: Skimming informational texts – Using superlative structures with adjectives
Week 8: Midterm Exam
Week 9: Listening to plans – Using the going to structure – Talking about future plans
Week 10: Reading notices and maps – Using prepositions of place – Writing descriptions of object locations
Week 11: Using a/an/the – Talking about cultural events
Week 12: Reading personal profiles and advertisements – Using can/can’t – Writing about personal skills
Week 13: Using will – Making future predictions
Week 14: Using should/shouldn’t – Writing advice texts
Week 15: Talking about free-time activities using (love/like/hate/enjoy) structures
Week 16: FINAL
Course Notes/Textbooks: Blackboard LMS - SFL materials

Course Objectives: The course provides a general approach for analysis of the foundation of the Republic of Turkey under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Emphasizing military, political, sociocultural and economic developments, the course seeks to compare the sectoral reforms of the Ottoman State during the period of the decline of the Empire with the farreaching, radical and revolutionary attempts made by Atatürk which paved the way for the establishment of modern and civilized institutions in Turkey between 1920 and 1938.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Describe the actors and factors that determine the history Analyze the different roles of these actors and factors Interpret the concepts of independence, freedom and national sovereignty Evaluate the process of formation of the contemporary, democratic, secular and social state of Turkey Understand the importance of national unity and cohesion. Explain the national goals and objectives of the Republic of Turkey. Solve the problems that Turkish society will face with an Atatürkist approach.
Course Description: This course provides a general information of the events from the end of the 19. century until the end of the Turkish War of Independence and the signing of the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 and the following period until 1990’s.
Week 1: Course aim and related words
Week 2: The Reasons of the Collapse of Ottoman State   Ottoman Reforms
Week 3: The State of the Ottoman Empire in the Early 20th Century
Week 4: World War I and the Fall of the Ottoman Empire
Week 5: Ottoman State after Mudros Armistice
Week 6: Preparation for The National Struggle
Week 7: Opening and Works of the Turkish Grand National Assembly
Week 8: Midterm Exam
Week 9: Lausenne Peace Agreement and Political Reforms
Week 10: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 11: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 12: Foreign Policy of Atatürk Period  (1923-1938)
Week 13: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
Week 14: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
15: Review of the Semester
16: Review of the Semester
Course Notes/Textbooks: Hasan Mert, Nuri Karakaş, vd., Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Tarihi, Editör: Elçin Yılmaz, İzmir Ekonomi Üniversitesi Y ayınları, 2024.

Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to show the students characteristics and rules of Turkish Language through examples; make them achieve the habit and skill of showing their emotions, thoughts, plans, impressions, observations, and experiences efficiently in writing and verbally; develop their vocabulary with the help of written and verbal texts; teach them the rules of comprehending the texts they read or programs they listen to accurately; develop their language skills which form the basis of the communication between individuals and populace.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; understand the rules of written expression, gain the ability to express their ideas effectively. learn the words forming sentences and recognize the importance of syntax. gain reading habit and read the book or attend events where comments from their perspective. acquire the stages of preparing scientific writing (collecting data, showing references, etc.). use communication tools -the form of petitions, official report, letters, etc. -for future life.
Course Description: Students will be taught how to use the written and verbal communication tools accurately and efficiently in this course. Various types of verbal and written statements will be examined through a critical point of view by doing exercises on understanding, telling, reading, and writing. Punctuation and spelling rules, which are basis of written statement, will be taught and accurate usage of these rules for efficient and strong expression will be provided. As for verbal statement, students will be taught how to use the body language, use accent and intonation elaborately, and use presentation techniques.

Course Objectives: Students taking this course gain practical experience in the processes of problem identification, objective setting, data collection, data analysis, evaluation, and reporting in marketing research, which plays a crucial role in every stage of international trade. This course aims to equip students with analytical thinking skills and the ability to conduct scientific research.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; • will be able to do explain the marketing information system and decision-making mechanism, • will be able to prepare a draft that includes all stages of marketing research, • will be able to define the marketing research problem and objective for goods and services, • will be able to collect primary and secondary data in accordance with scientific validity and reliability,• • will be able to conduct parametric and non-parametric tests using SPSS software, • will be able to organize interviews and focus group studies within qualitative research, • will be able to present and report the data obtained from the marketing research.

Frequently used in export and import processes, marketing research provides students with practical competence in managing qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods. In this course, students will mainly conduct practical training in a computer lab, where they will carry out their own marketing research projects.

Course Objectives: This course aims to enable students to effectively use, analyze, and evaluate promotional activities, such as advertising, public relations, sales promotion, direct marketing, personal selling, and digital marketing, at both practical and theoretical levels within the processes of international trade (export, import). Throughout the course, students will design a promotion campaign in foreign trade, exploring ways to ensure cultural compatibility and gain a competitive advantage in the international arena. This course emphasizes the importance of digitalization and cultural awareness for success in global trade, encouraging students to put these skills into practice.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; will be able to define promotional activities and strategies, will be able to design branding and brand management processes, will be able to select promotional tools based on the product, target audience, and industry characteristics, will be able to develop promotional strategies considering cultural differences, will be able to implement promotional methods in digital marketing and social media channels, will be able to plan and execute promotional campaigns.

It covers the use of digital marketing tools, strategies for different cultural markets, and the management of promotional activities on an international scale. Students create successful campaigns by utilizing both digital and traditional promotional tools tailored to the cultural characteristics of the target market. Additionally, the course equips students with the skills to engage in strategic planning on digital marketing platforms and social media channels, develop customized solutions based on cultural differences, and analyze the impact of these activities.

Course Objectives: This course aims to prepare students for university education and campus life, while guiding them to develop the academic, social, and personal skills they will need throughout their university education.

Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to provide students with reading, writing, listening and speaking skills at the beginner level (A1 level) in English language.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Communicate at a basic level by asking and answering simple questions Answer questions about very short, simple texts by scanning for specific information, Write a short text including an email, a postcard and a paragraph of present activities by giving information about themselves and/or their immediate surroundings, Fill in forms with personal details, Recognise familiar words and very basic phrases about themselves, their family and immediate surroundings in a simple speech spoken at a slow pace.
Course Description: This is a compulsory English course which provides basic language skills such as reading, writing, listening and speaking at the beginning level.
Week 1: Introduction to the course
Week 2: Introduce oneself and others-Identify names, surnames, occupations from texts-Use greetings, list countries, numbers 0–30
Week 3: Extract names, countries from conversations-Use greetings and introductions with correct stress-Write basic personal information accurately
Week 4: Use have got and possessive adjectives-Identify key points in music texts	-Use nationality words and days of the week
Week 5: Recognize days, music types, languages, countries-Introduce self using "I am" / "I have got"-Write a forum introduction with correct structures
Week 6: Form present simple (I, you, we, they)-Identify family info in texts-Name family members and belongings
Week 7: Recognize family relationships-Describe family and answer questions clearly-Write about family using relevant vocabulary
Week 8: Use present simple (he, she, it); adverbs-Extract routine data from timetables-Use time phrases, daily routine words
Week 9: Extract routine details from conversations-Share someone’s routine using intonation-Describe routines using sequence and time words
Week 10: Use quantifiers with countable/uncountable nouns-Identify ingredients from recipes-Name food, meals, and drinks
Week 11: Recognize food and drinks in dialogue-Discuss meals clearly and naturally-Write about a favorite meal
Week 12: Use there is/are and prepositions of place-Identify room details in texts-Name furniture, rooms, town places
Week 13: Extract data on places and rooms-Describe rooms and towns with spatial accuracy-Write a room/town description
Week 14: Use present continuous -Extract product details from ads- Use clothing and shopping words
Week 15: Recognize clothing items and numbers-Describe clothing using present continuous-Write outfit descriptions
Week 16: Final Exam

Assistant(s): -
Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to teach students general English at an elementary level (A1 – A2). By the end of the course, the students will have learned to understand and use present simple, present continuous and past simple tenses in communicative contexts. They will be able to skim and scan simple texts on a variety of topics and write a paragraph of 100-120 words on common topics. They will be able to ask and give information and give simple descriptions of people, things and places.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; communicate in simple and routine tasks and exchange information on familiar topics; read and understand short, simple texts and search for specific information; write an email, a postcard or  a short text to give information about present and past activities; catch the main point / missing parts in short, clear and simple messages or dialogues.
Course Description: This is a compulsory English course which provides basic language skills such as reading, writing, listening and speaking at the beginning level.
Week 1: Guessing the meaning of unknown words (childhood diaries, photo captions, memory notes) – Describing people, places, and times in the past – Writing a short paragraph about childhood
Week 2: Listening for main ideas and details (museum guides, short talks) – Using regular past tense verbs
Week 3: Skimming texts and identifying references (journals, event texts) – Talking about the past using irregular verbs
Week 4: Listening for main ideas and inferences (news, interviews) – Forming questions in the past tense
Week 5: Reading comparison texts – Distinguishing between past and present tenses – Writing a comparison of two communication tools
Week 6: Making inferences – Using comparative adjectives – Comparing objects orally
Week 7: Skimming informational texts – Using superlative structures with adjectives
Week 8: Midterm Exam
Week 9: Listening to plans – Using the going to structure – Talking about future plans
Week 10: Reading notices and maps – Using prepositions of place – Writing descriptions of object locations
Week 11: Using a/an/the – Talking about cultural events
Week 12: Reading personal profiles and advertisements – Using can/can’t – Writing about personal skills
Week 13: Using will – Making future predictions
Week 14: Using should/shouldn’t – Writing advice texts
Week 15: Talking about free-time activities using (love/like/hate/enjoy) structures
Week 16: FINAL

Course Objectives: Skills such as self-awareness, self-expression, and developing effective relationships for the socio-cultural structure are the objectives of this course. Therefore, theoretical and practical training is provided to ensure that our students acquire competencies in written, verbal, and non-verbal communication, which they will need in their career lives.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; explain the concept of communication and its relationship with other scientific disciplines, define the communication process along with its elements, explain linear, circular, and spiral communication models, classify types of written, verbal, and non-verbal communication, evaluate types of intrapersonal, interpersonal, and cultural communication, identify rhetoric-based persuasion strategies, make face-to-face presentations using effective communication methods.
Course Description: This course consists of content derived from fields related to communication, such as psychology, sociology, anthropology, and linguistics, as well as sector-based case analyses.

Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to understand the theoretical and practical aspects of social media, effectively use digital communication tools, examine the impact of social media platforms on individuals and businesses, and develop skills to create successful social media strategies. Additionally, the course aims to provide knowledge about the effects of social media on content management, community building, and personal and corporate brand management.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; will be able to interpret the impact of social media on individuals and interpersonal relations, will be able to explain the importance of new media for brands, will be able to discuss the role of social media in digital communication, will be able to evaluate the role of social media in intercultural interactions, will be able to define the role of social media in digital marketing, will be able to manage social media campaigns.
Course Description: This course examines the development of social media, its key concepts, and its role in today’s digital world. It provides students with fundamental knowledge on how social media platforms function, content creation, sharing, community management, and the development of social media strategies. Additionally, the course covers topics such as the individual, corporate, and societal impacts of social media, digital marketing, data analytics, and ethical issues. The course aims to offer both theoretical knowledge and practical experience through hands-on applications.

Course Objectives: The course provides a general approach for analysis of the foundation of the Republic of Turkey under the leadership of Mustafa Kemal Atatürk. Emphasizing military, political, sociocultural and economic developments, the course seeks to compare the sectoral reforms of the Ottoman State during the period of the decline of the Empire with the farreaching, radical and revolutionary attempts made by Atatürk which paved the way for the establishment of modern and civilized institutions in Turkey between 1920 and 1938.
Learning Outcomes: The students who succeeded in this course; Describe the actors and factors that determine the history Analyze the different roles of these actors and factors Interpret the concepts of independence, freedom and national sovereignty Evaluate the process of formation of the contemporary, democratic, secular and social state of Turkey Understand the importance of national unity and cohesion. Explain the national goals and objectives of the Republic of Turkey. Solve the problems that Turkish society will face with an Atatürkist approach.
Course Description: This course provides a general information of the events from the end of the 19. century until the end of the Turkish War of Independence and the signing of the Treaty of Lausanne in 1923 and the following period until 1990’s.
Week 1: Course aim and related words
Week 2: The Reasons of the Collapse of Ottoman State   Ottoman Reforms
Week 3: The State of the Ottoman Empire in the Early 20th Century
Week 4: World War I and the Fall of the Ottoman Empire
Week 5: Ottoman State after Mudros Armistice
Week 6: Preparation for The National Struggle
Week 7: Opening and Works of the Turkish Grand National Assembly
Week 8: Midterm Exam
Week 9: Lausenne Peace Agreement and Political Reforms
Week 10: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 11: Turkish Revolutions In Ataturk Era and Principles Of Ataturk
Week 12: Foreign Policy of Atatürk Period  (1923-1938)
Week 13: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
Week 14: Turkish Political Life in the Period 1939-1960
15: Review of the Semester
16: Review of the Semester
Course Notes/Textbooks: Hasan Mert, Nuri Karakaş, vd., Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Tarihi, Editör: Elçin Yılmaz, İzmir Ekonomi Üniversitesi Y ayınları, 2024.
Suggested Readings/Materials: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, Nutuk, Atatürk Araştırma Merkezi, Ankara 2005 Bernard Lewis, Modern Türkiye’nin Doğuşu, Ankara, 2017 Lord Kinross, Atatürk, İstanbul, 1981 Mahmut Goloğlu, Devrimler ve Tepkileri, İstanbul, 2009
